terra.problem: Saying David isn't lost asserts something the psalm doesn't establish.
The psalm records David's prayer but doesn't say whether he takes matters into his own hands.
Saying David leaves the matter with God adds what he does afterward, which the text doesn't establish.
David's kingship is a fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The payroll joke presents a modern employment detail as though it were a fact about David.
The writer says his mouth is filled with praise all day long, not that praise never runs out.
The quoted words are not the whole line. The enemies also call for him to be pursued and seized.
The crumb comparison doesn't work: crumbs under a counter are finite, so there is an end to counting them.
Someone can talk all day about something seen only once. That claim doesn't follow from the text.
The writer's amazement is presented as a fact rather than Papa Dorin's impression.
The writer's heart being full of wonder is an unmarked guess about his feeling.
Being brought back to life gives a specific interpretation of 'revive' that the verse leaves open.
